practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following eras marks the ascension of Kushana ruler Kanishka to the throne in 78 CE?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Saka Era began in 78 CE and is widely believed to have been founded by Kanishka, the most prominent ruler of the Kushana dynasty. It is also the basis of India's national calendar (the Saka calendar). Vikram Samvat started in 57 BCE, and the Gupta Era began in 319-320 CE. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History / Standard Historical Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: The National Calendar of India, introduced in 1957, is based on which of the following timekeeping systems?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Government of India adopted the Saka era-based calendar with a normal year of 365 days, starting from Chaitra 1, which corresponds to March 22 in a normal year and March 21 in a leap year. It was recommended by the Calendar Reform Committee headed by Meghnad Saha. [Primary Reference: NCERT / Government of India Guidelines]

practiceQuestions.q: Vikram Samvat, one of the most popular eras in India, is traditionally believed to have been established by which ruler?
practiceQuestions.sol: Vikram Samvat begins in 57 BCE and is traditionally associated with the victory of King Vikramaditya of Ujjain over the Shakas. It is a luni-solar calendar widely used in northern and western parts of India. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary characteristic of a lunisolar calendar, such as the traditional Indian calendar?
opts: It tracks only the phases of the moon.
It tracks only the movement of the sun.
Months are based on lunar cycles, while years are adjusted to solar years using intercalary months.
It follows a strict 365-day solar cycle without any moon tracking.
practiceQuestions.sol: Lunisolar calendars synchronize lunar months with the solar year. Since twelve lunar months fall short of a solar year by about 11 days, an intercalary month (Adhika Masa) is periodically added to keep the calendar aligned with the seasons. [Primary Reference: Standard Chronology & Astronomy Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: The Gupta Era (Gupta Samvat) was initiated in which of the following years CE?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Gupta Era commenced around 319-320 CE, marking the ascension of Chandragupta I to the Gupta throne. It was widely used in inscriptions and documents throughout the Gupta period. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: Harsha Era, started by King Harshavardhana of Kannauj, commenced in which year?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Harsha Era begins in 606 CE, coinciding with the coronation of Harshavardhana. It was used in parts of northern India during his reign and shortly thereafter. [Primary Reference: Standard Historical Texts on Ancient India]

practiceQuestions.q: In the traditional Indian calendar, what is the name of the first month of the lunar year?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chaitra is the first month of the Saka and traditional Indian lunisolar calendars, corresponding to March-April in the Gregorian calendar. The national calendar also begins with Chaitra 1. [Primary Reference: NCERT Art and Culture]

practiceQuestions.q: The Hijri Era, used in the Islamic calendar, is anchored to which major historical event?
opts: The migration of Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Medina (Hijra)
practiceQuestions.sol: The Hijri Era began in 622 CE, marking the Hijra—the migration of Prophet Muhammad and his followers from Mecca to Medina. It is a strictly lunar calendar consisting of 12 months in a year of 354 or 355 days. [Primary Reference: Standard Islamic History Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: Kollam Era (Malayalam Era), widely used in Kerala, commenced in which year CE?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Kollam Era or Malayalam Era commenced in 825 CE. It is traditionally associated with the foundation of the city of Kollam or the rebuilding of Quilon, and is extensively used in Kerala for agricultural and cultural calendars. [Primary Reference: Kerala History & Cultural Heritage Texts]

practiceQuestions.q: In a traditional Hindu lunar month, what is the fortnight associated with the waxing moon (bright fortnight) called?
practiceQuestions.sol: A lunar month is divided into two fortnights (pakshas): Shukla Paksha (the bright fortnight when the moon waxes from new moon to full moon) and Krishna Paksha (the dark fortnight when the moon wanes from full moon to new moon). [Primary Reference: NCERT Art & Culture]

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the Calendar Reform Committee (1952-53), headed by Meghnad Saha, established by the Government of India?
opts: To completely replace the Gregorian calendar with the Islamic Hijri calendar for administrative uniformity.
To establish a uniform national calendar across the country to overcome the multiplicity of regional calendars.
To abolish all indigenous eras and adopt the British colonial calendar permanently.
To synchronize the Gregorian calendar with the Mayan long-count calendar.
practiceQuestions.sol: At the time of independence, India had over thirty different calendars varying across regions, making national planning, administrative coordination, and gazette publication complex. The Meghnad Saha Committee standardized the Saka era-based calendar for uniform national usage. [Primary Reference: Scientific & Industrial Research / Historical Archives]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the traditional Indian lunisolar calendar account for the discrepancy between the lunar year and the solar year?
opts: By adding an extra day every four years like the leap year.
By inserting an intercalary month (Adhika Masa) approximately every 32-33 months.
By dropping two months every decade.
By ignoring solar alignment entirely and following moon phases only.
practiceQuestions.sol: A lunar year (12 lunar months) is roughly 354 days long, whereas a solar year is about 365 days long. This creates a deficit of roughly 11 days per year. To prevent festivals from shifting through all seasons, an extra month known as Adhika Masa or Purushottama Masa is added roughly every 2.7 years. [Primary Reference: NCERT Art & Culture / Traditional Astronomy]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary difference between the 'Amanta' and 'Purnimanta' systems in Indian chronological traditions?
opts: Amanta ends the month on a full moon, while Purnimanta ends it on a new moon.
Amanta ends the month on a new moon (Amavasya), while Purnimanta ends it on a full moon (Purnima).
Amanta is a purely solar system, whereas Purnimanta is purely Islamic.
Amanta is used only in South India, while Purnimanta is a Gregorian classification.
practiceQuestions.sol: In the Amanta (or Amavasyanta) system, followed mostly in southern and western India, a lunar month ends with the new moon (Amavasya). In the Purnimanta system, prevalent in northern India, a lunar month ends with the full moon (Purnima). [Primary Reference: Indian Epigraphy & Chronology Studies]

practiceQuestions.q: Why are indigenous Indian eras like Vikram Samvat and Saka Era of immense significance in archaeological and epigraphical studies?
opts: They provide precise chronological anchors for dating ancient inscriptions, copper plates, and royal decrees.
They were used exclusively for calculating tax rates in the British colonial treasury.
They eliminate the need for carbon-14 dating by measuring lunar gravity.
They were standardized by the United Nations to regulate global shipping lanes.
practiceQuestions.sol: Epigraphy relies heavily on eras mentioned in inscriptions to reconstruct political histories, trace dynasties, and correlate events across different regions. Eras like Saka and Vikram Samvat frequently appear on royal epigraphs. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / Epigraphia Indica]

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the relationship between the Saka Era and the Indian National Calendar. Which statement best explains their synchronization?
opts: The national calendar adopts the Saka year count but uses Gregorian month lengths.
The national calendar adopts the Saka year and traditional month names (Chaitra to Phalguna) synchronized with the solar tropical year.
The national calendar uses the Vikram Samvat year count with Islamic month structures.
It is completely independent of the Saka Era and follows the Babylonian calendar.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indian National Calendar retains the Saka era year numbering (with 78 CE as year 0/1) and traditional month names, but has fixed lengths for months corresponding to the tropical solar year to maintain alignment with the Gregorian calendar (e.g., Chaitra 1 always falling on March 22). [Primary Reference: Report of the Calendar Reform Committee / Ministry of Information and Broadcasting]

practiceQuestions.q: How do traditional Indian calendars reflect the synthesis of astronomy (Jyotisha) and cultural life?
opts: By linking agricultural seasons, solstices, equinoxes, and religious festivals to planetary and lunar movements.
By completely ignoring astronomical observations in favor of arbitrary royal proclamations.
By scheduling all economic taxation strictly according to solar eclipses.
By relying solely on weekly tidal shifts in coastal regions.
practiceQuestions.sol: Traditional Indian timekeeping is deeply rooted in 'Jyotisha' (one of the Vedangas). Calendars are meticulously calculated based on sidereal or tropical positions of the sun, moon, and constellations (nakshatras), tying agricultural harvests, equinoxes, solstices, and major festivals to precise astronomical markers. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / History of Science in India]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the Buddha Nirvana Era or Mahaparinirvana Era in ancient Indian chronology?
opts: It marks the birth of Gautama Buddha and was used by Ashoka in his edicts.
It is based on the passing away (parinirvana) of Gautama Buddha and was historically used in Buddhist texts and inscriptions.
It was established by Kanishka to commemorate the Fourth Buddhist Council.
It is a modern era invented in the 20th century for tourism purposes.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Buddha Nirvana era is anchored to the death (Mahaparinirvana) of Gautama Buddha. While historical exactitude of the date varies (traditionally placed around 543 BCE in Southeast Asian Theravada traditions or earlier by modern scholarship), it served as an important chronological framework in Buddhist monastic and epigraphical records. [Primary Reference: Ancient Indian History & Epigraphy Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: Why do regional variations exist in the celebration dates of certain pan-Indian festivals (e.g., New Year festivals like Gudi Padwa, Ugadi, Bihu, and Puthandu)?
opts: Because different regions follow distinct calendar systems (such as solar vs. lunisolar, or Amanta vs. Purnimanta).
Because kings in medieval times arbitrarily changed festival dates to suit their administrative whims.
Due to differences in Gregorian time zones across Indian states.
Because ancient texts prohibited celebrating festivals on the same day nationwide.
practiceQuestions.sol: Regional New Year celebrations across India—such as Gudi Padwa in Maharashtra, Ugadi in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, Puthandu in Tamil Nadu, and Bihu in Assam—coincide with the transition of the sun into Aries (Mesha Sankranti) or the beginning of the Chaitra month in lunisolar calendars, reflecting differences in solar vs. lunisolar calculations and regional traditions. [Primary Reference: NCERT Art & Culture / Cultural Geography of India]

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of Indian chronology, what is 'Sankranti'?
opts: The lunar eclipse caused by the shadow of the Earth.
The transition of the sun from one zodiac sign (rasi) to another.
The intercalary month added every three years.
The conclusion of a 60-year Jovian cycle.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sankranti refers to the transition (movement) of the Sun from one zodiac sign (Rashi) to the next in the Indian astronomical zodiac. There are 12 Sankrantis in a solar year, with Makar Sankranti (transition into Capricorn) being the most widely celebrated across India. [Primary Reference: Traditional Indian Astronomy & Panchang Canons]

practiceQuestions.q: What role does the 60-year Jupiter cycle (Brihaspati Samvatsara) play in traditional Indian timekeeping?
opts: It tracks the orbital period of Jupiter relative to Saturn for tax collection.
It acts as a larger chronological cycle consisting of 60 uniquely named years, repeating in a perpetual loop.
It is used exclusively to determine leap seconds in the Saka calendar.
It marks the exact duration of an emperor's reign in ancient India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 60-year cycle is based on the approximate conjunction of Jupiter's 12-year orbital period and Saturn's 30-year orbital period (lowest common multiple). Each of the 60 years has a specific Sanskrit name and is used in Panchangs for astrological and long-term chronological tracking. [Primary Reference: Indian Astronomical Treatises / Surya Siddhanta]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding traditional Indian eras and calendars:
1. The Vikram Samvat precedes the Saka Era by 135 years.
2. The Saka Era was founded by Emperor Kanishka in 78 CE and is the basis of India's National Calendar.
3. The Gupta Era commenced in 319-320 CE, coinciding with the ascension of Chandragupta I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Vikram Samvat starts in 57 BCE, and Saka Era starts in 78 CE. The difference is 57 + 78 = 135 years. Statement 2 is correct: Saka Era began in 78 CE, associated with Kanishka, and was adopted as India's National Calendar in 1957. Statement 3 is correct: Gupta Era started in 319-320 CE with Chandragupta I's coronation. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History & Standard Historical Texts]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian National Calendar:
1. It is based on the Saka era with Chaitra as its first month.
2. A normal year in this calendar has 365 days, exactly matching the Gregorian calendar months in duration.
3. The dates of the National Calendar have a permanent correspondence with the dates of the Gregorian calendar (e.g., Chaitra 1 always corresponds to March 22 in a normal year).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The National Calendar uses the Saka era and begins with Chaitra 1. Statement 2 is incorrect because the lengths of the months in the National Calendar (e.g., Chaitra has 30 days in a normal year and 31 in a leap year, Vaisakha to Jyestha have 31 days) do not match the uneven month lengths of the Gregorian calendar. Statement 3 is correct: There is a permanent correspondence (Chaitra 1 is March 22 in normal years and March 21 in leap years). [Primary Reference: Report of the Calendar Reform Committee]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Lunisolar calendars in India:
1. In a lunisolar calendar, months are determined by the lunar cycle, while the year is adjusted to the solar year.
2. The 'Adhika Masa' (intercalary month) is added periodically to reconcile the 11-day deficit between the lunar and solar years.
3. The Purnimanta system, where a month ends on the full moon, is exclusively practiced in southern India while Amanta is practiced in the north.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Lunisolar calendars use lunar months and adjust via Adhika Masa to account for the ~11-day annual drift against the solar year. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Purnimanta system is prevalent in northern India, whereas the Amanta (Amavasyanta) system is prevalent in southern and western India. [Primary Reference: NCERT Art & Culture]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following historical eras with their corresponding founding years:
1. Vikram Samvat : 57 BCE
2. Saka Era : 78 CE
3. Gupta Era : 319 CE
4. Harsha Era : 606 CE
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
practiceQuestions.sol: All four pairs are correctly matched. Vikram Samvat began in 57 BCE, Saka Era in 78 CE, Gupta Era in 319-320 CE, and Harsha Era in 606 CE. These eras form the backbone of Indian epigraphical dating. [Primary Reference: Standard Epigraphical & Historical Canons]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Islamic and other regional Indian calendars:
1. The Islamic Hijri calendar is a pure lunar calendar consisting of 12 lunar months in a year of 354 or 355 days.
2. Because the Hijri calendar is purely lunar, its months rotate through all the seasons of the solar year over a ~33-year cycle.
3. The Kollam (Malayalam) Era used in Kerala is a pure solar calendar starting in 825 CE.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct. The Hijri calendar is strictly lunar (354-355 days), shifting through seasons across a ~33-year solar cycle. The Kollam Era (825 CE) used in Kerala is a sidereal solar calendar closely tied to the sun's passage through zodiac signs. [Primary Reference: Islamic Chronology & South Indian Epigraphy]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural parts of a traditional Indian Panchang (Calendar):
1. Tithi refers to a lunar day, representing the time taken by the moon to increase its longitudinal distance from the sun by 12 degrees.
2. Vara refers to the lunar month, while Nakshatra refers to the solar year.
3. Yoga and Karana are other vital components of a Panchang used to determine auspicious timings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: A tithi is a lunar day defined by the 12-degree separation between the sun and moon. Statement 2 is incorrect because 'Vara' means solar weekday (Monday, Tuesday, etc.), not the lunar month, and 'Nakshatra' refers to lunar mansions/constellations, not the solar year. Statement 3 is correct: Panchang has five limbs (Pancha-Anga): Tithi, Vara, Nakshatra, Yoga, and Karana. [Primary Reference: Traditional Jyotisha & Panchang Canons]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Calendar Reform Committee of 1952:
1. It was chaired by renowned astrophysicist Meghnad Saha.
2. The committee recommended discarding all regional calendars in favor of a uniform Gregorian calendar for all civil and religious purposes.
3. It recommended a uniform Saka-based national calendar with a fixed number of days and scientifically determined month lengths.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: The committee was headed by Meghnad Saha and proposed a scientifically structured Saka-based national calendar. Statement 2 is incorrect because the committee did not interfere with traditional religious calendars (Panchangs) used for socio-religious rituals; it only provided a uniform national calendar for official state purposes (like the Gazette of India). [Primary Reference: Report of the Calendar Reform Committee / CSIR]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding chronological eras in ancient India:
1. The Laukika Era (also known as the Saptarishi Era) is an ancient chronological system prevalent in Kashmir and neighboring regions, characterized by repeating 2700-year cycles.
2. The Mahavira Nirvana Era is used by the Jain community to commemorate the attainment of moksha by Lord Mahavira.
3. The Sri Harsha Era was adopted across southern peninsular kingdoms by the Cholas and Pandyas as their primary administrative era.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: The Laukika (Saptarishi) era was widely used in Kashmir with 2700-year cycles, and the Mahavira Nirvana era marks Mahavira's nirvana (527 BCE). Statement 3 is incorrect because the Harsha Era (606 CE) was confined primarily to northern India (Kanauj and surrounding areas) during and after Harshavardhana's reign, not southern peninsular kingdoms like Cholas and Pandyas (who used their own regnal years and Kollam era). [Primary Reference: Indian Epigraphy / D.C. Sircar]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the concept of 'Paksha' and lunar fortnights in Indian timekeeping:
1. Shukla Paksha is the bright fortnight when the moon transitions from full moon to new moon.
2. Krishna Paksha is the dark fortnight when the moon wanes from full moon to new moon.
3. Each Paksha consists of 15 tithis, corresponding to the phases of the lunar cycle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Shukla Paksha is the bright fortnight when the moon waxes from new moon (Amavasya) to full moon (Purnima). Statement 2 is correct: Krishna Paksha is the dark fortnight when the moon wanes from full moon to new moon. Statement 3 is correct: Each Paksha comprises 15 tithis (lunar days), making up the 30 tithis of a complete lunar month. [Primary Reference: NCERT Art & Culture / Traditional Astronomy]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the cultural and historical role of traditional Indian calendars:
1. Traditional calendars were essential not only for religious rituals and festivals but also for agricultural planning, monsoon tracking, and revenue collection.
2. The coexistence of multiple eras (such as Vikram, Saka, and regional eras) in Indian history reflects the decentralized political landscape and regional dynastic milestones.
3. The Gregorian calendar completely eradicated all indigenous Indian calendar systems from rural and spiritual spheres within a decade of British rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Calendars served vital socio-religious, agricultural, and administrative roles, and the multitude of eras reflects India's rich dynastic and regional history. Statement 3 is blatantly incorrect because indigenous calendar systems (Panchangs) and festivals continue to thrive across rural and spiritual spheres in India to this day, long outliving British colonial rule. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History / Sociological Studies of Indian Tradition]
